subject: Clarification: retention of invoices/usage records vs customer deletion requests
messages:
From: Jane Porter <jporter@acme.example.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on retention: invoices vs deletion requests

Hi Laura,

Quick question from our finance team: when a customer asks Redwood to delete their data under a data subject request, will Redwood still retain invoices and usage records (for our accounting and audit purposes)? Our accounting needs to keep invoice PDFs and amounts for tax/audit for several years, but we also have strict internal privacy rules to honor erasure requests.

Attached is an example invoice (invoice_20260301.pdf) — you can see the invoice lists a contact name and the last 4 digits of a payment method. Can Redwood satisfy erasure requests while keeping invoice/usage history for billing compliance? If there are nuances by region (EU VAT vs US tax) or a separate process we should follow, please advise.

Thanks — Jane
Jane Porter
Head of Finance, Acme Corp
attachments: invoice_20260301.pdf

From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Porter <jporter@acme.example.com>, billing@acme.example.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on retention: invoices vs deletion requests

Hi Jane — thanks for the note and the sample invoice. Short answer: yes, we can honor erasure requests while retaining accounting records, but there are operational steps and region-specific nuances. High-level: 

- Invoices and billing metadata (invoice numbers, amounts, tax lines) are kept as accounting records and can be retained per statutory requirements.
- We can remove or pseudonymize PII from billing attachments and raw usage payloads on request (e.g., contact names, email addresses in payloads).
- For usage logs: by default raw request payloads are retained for 90 days; aggregated usage metrics and billing exports are retained longer for reconciliation.

Next steps: I want to coordinate with our Finance and Legal teams to confirm retention windows by jurisdiction and to propose a redaction workflow (redact contact PII from invoices or replace with hashed IDs). I'll loop in Marissa and Rishi and come back with an exact plan and timeline.

Would you prefer we: (A) keep invoices as-is under a legal/accounting bucket, and remove PII from associated usage logs; or (B) produce redacted invoice PDFs that still contain invoice number/amount but remove contact PII? If you have procurement/controls that require the original invoice PDF for audit, call that out so we surface it to Legal.

Best,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of GTM Operations, Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Question on retention: invoices vs deletion requests — need finance/legal input

Team — forwarding Acme's question. Key points / what I think we need to confirm: 

1) System state: invoices are generated and stored in our billing service (billing-db + archived S3 bucket) and we also export per-customer usage CSVs monthly. Invoice PDFs are kept in s3/archive indefinitely by default for reconciliation. Raw request payloads (prompts/responses) live in request-logs for 90 days and then are rolled into a cold store for 2 years for internal debugging; we have a flag to delete raw payloads earlier per customer.

2) Requirement: Finance wants to retain invoice numbers, amounts, VAT lines, payment confirmations for audit for the statutory period. Legal needs to advise whether retaining full invoice PDFs with contact names conflicts with erasure requests in the EU.

3) Options: mark invoice records as accounting_records (immutable), or produce redacted invoice PDFs and keep original locked in a legal vault for court/regulatory requests; or hash customer_id on billing exports.

Marissa — can you confirm standard retention windows we should implement (US accounting X years, EU VAT country-specific)? Rishi — can billing team expose an option on the account to flag "redaction requested" so exported usage CSVs and linked invoices are transformed (PII removed) automatically?

If we get a deletion request from Acme's end-customer, we need a documented runbook: which tables to scrub, what we preserve (invoice metadata, hashed customer id), who approves archive access.

Thanks — Laura

From: marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Question on retention: invoices vs deletion requests — need finance/legal input

Laura / Rishi — quick legal/finance summary: 

- US: accounting best practice and IRS guidance suggest keeping tax/invoice records for 3–7 years depending on the record type; we typically retain invoices and payment confirmations for 7 years.
- EU: VAT and tax retention periods vary by country (example: Germany 10 years). GDPR does not automatically trump tax law — there are lawful-basis exceptions for retaining personal data necessary for compliance with legal obligations (e.g., tax). However, we should still minimize PII when possible and document the lawful basis.

Proposed approach we recommend implementing: 
1) Classify billing artifacts as accounting_records with a retention policy per-account that defaults to statutory minima (US 7 years; EU country-specific).
2) For deletion/erasure requests: redact PII from non-accounting stores (raw logs, model payloads). For invoices, either: (a) retain original invoice in an encrypted legal vault accessible only by Compliance/Legal, and provide the customer a redacted copy for their records; or (b) store only invoice metadata (invoice number, date, amount, VAT) in billing-db and remove contact PII if the customer requests it and there is no regulatory need for the PII.
3) Maintain an auditable trail (who approved retention beyond erasure request, timestamp, reason) — this is critical.

Action items: Rishi, please confirm technical feasibility and ETA for two features: (i) a per-account "enforce_redaction" toggle that will redact PII in future billing exports and (ii) a one-off redaction job for historic invoices/exports. Also add a label that marks records as "accounting_records" so they are handled differently in the erasure pipeline.

I can draft the written policy language for customers and a short FAQ that we can include in the contract.

— Marissa
Finance & Legal (acting)

From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Porter <jporter@acme.example.com>, billing@acme.example.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on retention: invoices vs deletion requests

Hi Jane — thanks for the patience while we pulled Finance & Legal in. Summary and proposed path forward: 

1) What we can retain: Redwood will keep invoice records and billing metadata required for accounting (invoice number, date, amounts, tax lines, payment status) for statutory retention periods (default: US 7 years; EU: country-specific VAT rules). These artifacts will be marked as accounting_records.

2) What we'll erase/redact: upon a data subject erasure request we will remove personal data from non-accounting stores (raw prompts/responses, request logs, backups that are not required for audit). For invoices and billing attachments we offer two options: (A) retain original in an encrypted legal vault accessible only to Compliance & Legal, while providing a redacted invoice to the customer; or (B) redact PII from the invoice PDF and store the redacted copy as the canonical copy for that customer. We will not delete invoice metadata required for accounting unless legally permitted.

3) Technical controls: we can enable a per-account redaction flag ("enforce_redaction") to ensure new exports and future invoices omit PII. For historic invoices we can run a one-time redaction job; timing depends on the volume (estimate: 2–6 weeks for a mid-sized account).

4) Audit trail & approvals: any retention beyond an erasure request will be recorded with justification (legal basis), approver, and timestamp.

Next steps: Please confirm which option you prefer for invoice handling (A or B) and whether you need Redwood to run a historic redaction job on prior invoices/exports. Once you confirm, we will open a ticket (JIRA-BILL-4123) and share a checklist and timeline.

Attaching: redwood-billing-retention-checklist.xlsx, redaction_playbook_v1.0.pdf

Best,
Laura
Head of GTM Operations, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-billing-retention-checklist.xlsx; redaction_playbook_v1.0.pdf
